steps: Check the fireplace & chimney

Masonry wood-burning fireplace only, never factory-built, with a chimney at least 15' from the hearth that serves no other appliance. Sweep and inspect the chimney and repair cracks, loose mortar or other defects before installing.

The fireplace must be built to N.F.P.A. 211 (latest edition) or applicable codes; the installation shall conform to CAN/CSA-B365. Check for creosote buildup or other obstructions. Check the opening against the minimum fireplace dimensions drawing (Figure 3, p. 13). No makeshift or temporary installation.

Pacific Energy recommends installers certified by NFI, CSIA, WETT or APC.
Prepare the fireplace

Lock the damper open or remove it; don't remove bricks or mortar, and fasten the supplied metal tag to the back wall if the fireplace was modified. Protect the hearth with cardboard or a heavy blanket; the insert is a two-person lift.

Exception (p. 16): masonry or steel, including the damper plate, may be removed from the smoke shelf and adjacent damper frame if needed to fit a chimney liner, provided this doesn't weaken the fireplace and chimney or reduce protection for combustibles below the National Building Code.
Run the liner

Canada: continuous liner from the flue collar to the chimney top, to the class 3 requirements of CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640; USA: UL-1777 liner or direct flue connection (p. 18). Feed it down through the damper area and fit a stove-to-liner adapter per the liner maker.

Full liner: measure from the top of the existing chimney flue to the hearth floor, allowing extra for flashing and rain cap. Feed the stainless steel liner from the top of the chimney, through the damper area, into the fireplace cavity.

Direct flue connection (USA only, p. 18): measure from the top of the first chimney flue tile to the top of the insert, allowing extra to enter the tile. Feed the liner through the damper area into the first flue tile, seal around it in the chimney throat, then follow steps 3-9 of the full-liner procedure. A clean-out door may be required by local code.

Pacific Energy highly recommends the full liner: the insert drafts correctly and avoids difficult start-ups and smoking out the door.
Fit the flue collar to the liner
The collar is packed in the stove: attach it to the liner adapter with three stainless screws. Caulk the connections with high temp stove cement and check the gasket.
Strip the insert
Lift and pull off the front trim, remove the backing plate (two T20 Torx screws each side), then remove the baffle (p. 11).

Baffle removal (p. 11): slide the ceramic board above the tubes toward the front and pull the retaining pin at the back of the firebox, under the baffle. Lift the baffle off the supply tube, move it to one side and tilt it down out of the firebox; you may need to remove the opposite brick rail (take out the brick under it, lift the rail up and inward off its pins). Inspect the baffle-to-supply-tube gasket (prt#80000365).

Reinstall in reverse: the two side blankets tight against the side rails, the ceramic board pushed back tight against the baffle.

Do not operate with the baffle assembly, tubes or insulation removed.
Set & level the insert

Push the unit into the fireplace and level it with the front or rear adjustment legs (in the bottom, sides, front and rear). If the fireplace floor is lower than the hearth, fit the rear leveling bolts first.

Rear leveling bolts (p. 14): prop the unit up to reach the threaded inserts under the sides toward the rear, thread in the supplied bolts and set them to the depth of the fireplace drop. Then push the insert into position and adjust the bolts to level it.

With outside air, don't cover the air inlet (p. 19).
Secure the collar

Reach through the flue opening and pull the collar down with the tool provided until the bolts pass through the mounting holes. Install the clamps and nuts, center the collar on the opening and tighten.
Flash & cap the chimney
Measure, trim and shape the chimney top flashing for a 1" to 1-1/2" overlap on each side and seat it firmly against the flue tile over the liner. Attach a rain cap; a storm collar is optional.
Combustion air

Outside air: replace the ash clean-out cover with a rodent screen, keep the insert's air inlet uncovered, then seal the surround to the fireplace and anywhere else air may enter. Otherwise air is drawn from the room through the front.
Power, backing plate & trim

Plug into a properly grounded three-prong outlet with the cord routed clear of the unit (it can exit right or left). Remove the speed knob, fit the backing plate with four screws, refit the knob, and hook the front trim into its slots with the tabs fully engaged.

Moving the cord to the left (p. 21): remove the front trim, speed knob and backing plate and disconnect the rocker-switch leads. Remove the two Torx T20 screws holding the electrical box and wiring cover under the ash shelf, move the strain relief to the left-side hole, then remount and reconnect the rocker-switch leads.

Front trim: line up the hooks on its back with the locking slots in the brackets on either side of the firebox (between the blower bracket and the door), push in, then slide down to engage.

panels.title: Dirty glass / excess creosote
items: Air control or damper turned down too soon → wait for a good bed of coals and charred wood
Draft too low: chimney plugged or restricted, improper height and/or diameter → inspect and clean; provide outside air for combustion
Door gasket leakage (dirty glass) → replace gasket; check latch

panels.title: Low heat output
items: Fire too small → build a larger fire
Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted; inspect and clean

panels.title: Won't burn overnight
items: Air control set too high → set it lower
Not enough wood → unsplit wood is preferred for overnight burns
Draft too high → excessive chimney height and/or diameter
Door gasket leaking → replace door gasket

panels.title: Stove won't burn
items: Combustion air supply blocked → check outside air supply for obstruction; check that room air cover is removed
Draft too low → chimney plugged or restricted, inspect and clean
Chimney oversized or otherwise unsuitable → consult dealer

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Build every fire directly on the firebricks, with the air control wide open.

  1. Slide the air control to High, all the way to the left, and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the center of the firebox. Crisscross several pieces of dry kindling over it, then add a few small pieces of dry wood on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" to 1" until the kindling is fully engulfed in flame. Don't leave the insert unattended while the door is open.
  4. Add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. Once there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, set the air control for normal burning.
Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or any other flammable liquid to start or freshen up a fire. Keep such liquids well away from the insert while it's in use.
First few fires: the paint is curing (baking on) and gives off smoke and fumes. Open all windows and doors so the room is well ventilated, and follow the Stove Bright sheet that came with the insert. Smoke detectors may go off more often for a while. Don't disconnect them.

burn.title: Air control, reloading & overnight burns
burn.html:
One lever controls the fire. Slide it left toward "H" (high) for more air, or right toward "L" (low) for less. The best setting depends on your wood, the weather and your chimney, so note what works for future fires.

  • If smoke pours down across the glass (a "waterfall"), you turned the air down too soon or too low.
  • Use "H" only to start a fire or get a fresh load going.
  • Keep the door closed while burning. Open it only to add wood.

Reloading

  1. Slide the air to high and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly so smoke doesn't puff back into the room.
  3. Load dry logs east/west (side to side), up to 18" long, with space between them for air. Don't load so high that opening the door becomes hazardous.

Overnight

Use unsplit logs, and char the load completely on the maximum setting before turning the air down. Don't try it with green or wet wood. To restart, rake the hot embers to the front, add a couple of dry split logs, close the door and set the air to high. Once the wood chars, reset the air.

The lowest burn rate is set at the factory. Altering it is against federal regulations.

wood.title: Choosing and testing your wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood generally burns more efficiently and cleanly than softwood or green, freshly cut wood.

  • Air-dry (season) wood for six months or more. Store it under cover, away from open flame or heat sources.
  • Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives very little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.

Test a piece

Add a large piece to a good, large bed of coals and watch:

Burning on more than one side within one minuteDry
Turns black and lights within three minutesDamp
Sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutesSoaked: don't burn it

Never burn

Garbage, treated wood, salt-water wood, coal or charcoal, cardboard and other paper products, plywood or particleboard, anything containing plastic, rubber or asbestos, yard waste, railroad ties, construction debris, manure, solvents, paints or petroleum products. They can give off toxic fumes, and charcoal can make deadly carbon monoxide. Salt-water wood and garbage contain chlorides that quickly destroy metal and void the warranty. Never barbecue in the insert.

Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting a fire.

blower.title: Running the blowers
blower.html:
The insert has twin variable-speed circulating air blowers. A rocker switch picks automatic or manual control, and the speed control sets how fast they run.

Rocker switch offAutomatic: the blowers start once the insert reaches operating temperature and stop after the fire is out and it has cooled
Rocker switch onManual: bypasses the temperature switch so you have full control

Suggested settings

  • Air control at "L" (low, pushed to the far right): run the blowers on low.
  • Air control anywhere above "L": any blower speed you like.

Keep them clean

At least every six months, vacuum the grill openings at the back and bottom of the blower casing to remove dust and debris.

Power: plug into a properly grounded three-prong outlet and never cut off the grounding prong. Keep the cord out from under the insert and away from hot or sharp surfaces. Disconnect power before servicing.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when the insert is cold, using fireplace glass cleaner. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape it with anything that could scratch.

What the deposit tells you

  • Light brown and dusty, wipes off easily: usually good combustion and dry, well-seasoned wood, so the pipes and chimney are likely relatively clean.
  • Black and greasy, hard to remove: wet or green wood and too slow a burn. That heavy deposit is building up at least as quickly in the chimney.

Protect it

  • Don't slam the door, and check that no logs stick out to hit the glass when you close it.
  • If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before you use the insert again. Use only 10-1/2" x 16-1/2" x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer.
  • Clean the plated door with mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Take ashes out only when the insert is cold.

  • When the ash gets 3" to 4" deep in the firebox, let the fire burn down and cool, then remove the excess.
  • Leave about 1" of ash on the firebox floor. It helps keep a hot charcoal bed.
  • Keep the front of the firebox, where boost combustion air comes in, clear of heavy ash so it doesn't block the airflow.

Disposal

Put the ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set the closed container on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn, until final disposal. If you bury or scatter the ashes, keep them in the closed container until all the cinders have thoroughly cooled. Don't put any other waste in that container.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow, smoky fires leave creosote in the chimney. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot: over 2000°F inside the chimney.

  • Inspect the chimney and connector at least once every two months during the heating season. Remove creosote once it is 3 mm or more.
  • Check daily until experience shows how often you need to clean. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.
  • Keep it down with dry, seasoned wood and small loads (two or three logs, or 1/4 to 1/2 of a full load), with the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after each loading.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Get everyone ready to leave, with a meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air control on the insert.
  3. Call the fire department, and keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Before the next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks. Check the combustibles around the chimney and the roof too.

maint.title: Gasket, baffle & routine checks
maint.html:
Check these parts for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and excessive warping. If you find damage, contact your dealer: running the insert with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty.

WeeklyFirebrick (cracking); door gasket (sagging, placement, damage)
MonthlyBrick rails and their tabs; air riser tube at the back of the firebox; back of the airwash chamber; baffle locking pin; baffle tubes
When the chimney is cleanedTop baffle board / blanket; baffle; top heat shield and bolts; baffle gasket; brick rails; manifold

Door gasket

The door seals with 7/8" medium density fiberglass rope that needs only light pressure. Keep it in good condition and replace it when needed with the kit from your Pacific Energy dealer.

Confirm the gasket part number: the manual gives the gasket kit as prt# 80000156 on p. 9 and lists the Neo 1.6 door gasket as 80000670 on p. 26.

Baffle

Some baffle warping is normal, up to 1/4". Replace it if it is permanently warped more than that, cracked or broken. Never run the insert with the baffle, tubes or insulation removed.

Use only materials supplied by the manufacturer for maintenance and replacements.

safety.title: Safety & overfiring
safety.html:
• The insert is hot while it runs, especially its outside surfaces. Keep children, clothing and furniture away; contact can burn skin.
  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning. The insert isn't designed for open-door burning; sparks, embers or smoke can come out.
  • Burn directly on the firebricks, never on a grate or andirons. Replace broken or missing bricks.
  • Never alter the air control assembly. Tampering is hazardous and voids the warranty.
  • Keep wood, furniture, newspapers and other loose combustibles out of the clearance area and the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Teach everyone in the house how to run the insert safely and what to do in a chimney fire.
Don't overfire it. A glowing red top or vent pipe means it's overfiring, which can permanently damage the insert and chimney and may void the warranty. An uncontrollable burn or glowing red parts also point to too much draft.
Pacific Energy strongly recommends smoke and carbon monoxide detectors in the area where the insert is installed. Smoke leaking into the room through joints points to too little draft.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's Limited Lifetime Wood Products Warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Ltd lifetime (10 years)Parts only: porcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage, not impact), plating, firebox and baffle
3 year comprehensiveParts and labor on any defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Labor under the lifetime coverage.
  • Firebox rails and heat shields (outside the lifetime coverage); firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets (not warranted).
  • Any part showing misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification.

Excessive draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel (high sodium, plastics, chemicals) may void it. Tampering with the air control or using abrasive cleaners on the plated door will; overfiring may.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. You can register the insert at pacificenergy.net/register; the serial number is on the certification label or the manual cover.

This is a summary. The full terms are in the manual.

specEff.title: Emissions, efficiency & heat output
specEff.html:
EPA certified emissions1.9 grams per hour
HHV tested efficiency72%
LHV tested efficiency78%
EPA BTU output13,494 to 23,186 btu/hr.

Meets the 2020 EPA crib wood particulate emission standards (Method 28R). Efficiencies are weighted averages tested to CSA B415; the BTU range uses the burn rates from the low and high EPA tests with Douglas Fir dimensional lumber. The rating statement on the same page rounds it to 13,500 to 23,200 Btu/hr.

The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered (federal regulations, p. 7).

specWood.title: Fuel & wood length
specWood.html:
FuelSeasoned cord wood
Maximum wood length18 inches
Ideal wood length16-17 inches
LoadingEast/west

Normal Operation (p. 7) gives the same limit: up to 18"(457mm). Solid fuel (cordwood) only. Build the fire directly on the firebricks; no grate, andirons or elevated fire.

specFlue.title: Chimney, liner & draft
specFlue.html:
Flue collar6" I.D., removable
Chimney height (from hearth)15' (minimum)
Recommended draft.06" w.c. – .09" w.c. when hot, on high
CanadaFull liner to the chimney top, class 3 requirements of CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640
USAFlue liner conforming to UL-1777, or direct flue connection

Masonry wood-burning fireplace only; do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance. Lock the damper open or remove it. Direct flue connection (USA only, p. 18): liner into the first flue tile with a seal in the chimney throat; a clean-out door may be required by local code. Pacific Energy highly recommends a full liner for correct draft and to prevent difficult start-ups and smoking out the door.

Too much draft shows as an uncontrollable burn or glowing red parts; too little as back puffing or smoke leaking from appliance and connector joints (p. 8).

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Side of door to adjacent sidewall13 in.
Side of door to side facing (max 3-1/2 in. deep)9.5 in.
Top of front brow to mantel facing13 in.
Top of front brow to mantel (max 12 in. deep)13 in.

The rating label (p. 3) gives the same inch values: side clearances measured from the side of the door, top facing and mantel from the insert surround brow.

Confirm the metric clearances: the manual gives 13 in. (255 mm.), 9.5 in. (155 mm.) and 13 in. (305 mm.) in the clearance table on p. 15, but 330 MM / 13 IN, 240 MM / 9.5 IN and 330 MM / 13IN on the rating label (p. 3), and 13" / 330mm and 9 1/2" / 240mm in Figure 5 (p. 15).
Confirm the fireplace type: p. 15 lists these clearances "when installed into a masonry or factory built fireplace"; the rating label (p. 3) and p. 16 say the insert is not to be installed in a factory-built fireplace.

specHearth.title: Hearth & ember protection
specHearth.html:
Masonry hearth16" in front, 8" beyond each side of the fireplace opening
Ember protection, USA16" to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the door opening
Ember protection, Canada18" to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the unit

Ember protection is non-combustible material over combustible flooring in front of the insert. The rating label (p. 3) also requires a non-combustible hearth under the unit extending 16IN / 406MM in front of the fireplace opening face. Codes: N.F.P.A. 211 (USA), CAN/CSA-B365 (Canada). Figure 4 (p. 14) shows the ember protection as a dimensioned drawing.

specAir.title: Combustion air
specAir.html:
Outside airThrough the fireplace ash clean-out to the intake on the bottom of the appliance
Room airDrawn from the room through the front of the unit

Consult local building codes. For outside air, remove the ash clean-out cover and put a rodent screen in its place, set the insert without covering the air inlet, and when installation is complete seal the surround to the fireplace and anywhere else air may enter.

The troubleshooting chart (p. 22) lists a blocked combustion air supply as a cause of the stove not burning: check the outside air supply for obstruction and check that the room air cover is removed.

specElec.title: Electrical (blowers)
specElec.html:
Rating label (p. 3)115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP
Electrical Supply (p. 20)120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A
OutletProperly grounded, accepts a three-pronged plug
Confirm the voltage: the manual gives 115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP on the rating label (p. 3) and 120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A for the circulating air blowers on p. 20.

Don't cut or remove the grounding prong. Don't route the cord under the unit; keep it clear of hot or sharp surfaces. Follow local codes or, in their absence, CSA C22.2 (Canada) or ANSI/NFPA 70 (USA). The cord can be moved to exit on the left side (p. 21). Disconnect power before servicing.

conflicts.issue: Metric clearance values disagree. The p. 15 table gives 13 in.(255 mm.) side of door to adjacent sidewall, 9.5 in.(155 mm.) to side facing and 13 in.(305 mm.) brow to mantel / mantel facing; the rating label (p. 3) gives 330 MM / 13 IN, 240 MM / 9.5 IN and 330 MM / 13IN, and Figure 5 (p. 15) shows 13" 330mm and 9 1/2" 240mm. Inch values agree everywhere.

p. 15 introduces the clearances 'when installed into a masonry or factory built fireplace'; the rating label (p. 3) says 'NOT TO BE INSTALLED IN A FACTORY-BUILT FIREPLACE' and p. 16 says 'This Insert shall not be installed in a factory-built fireplace.'
Electrical rating is 115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP on the rating label (p. 3) but 120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A in Electrical Supply (p. 20).
Door gasket part number: the maintenance text names the gasket kit prt# 80000156 (p. 9); the parts list gives 'Gasket, Door, NEO 1.6' as 80000670 (p. 26).

catalog_mismatches.manual: Maximum Wood Length 18 inches (p. 3); 'up to 18"(457mm)' in Normal Operation (p. 7)

review.notes: Model naming: p. 2 says the manual describes the 'VISTA INSERT LE' and Figure 11 (p. 23) is captioned 'Vista Insert LE - Firebrick layout'; the cover, rating label, footers and parts list say NEO 1.6 INSERT LE, which the guide follows. Cross-reference slips: p. 13 hearth text says 'See Figure 2' (the opening drawing is Figure 3); p. 15 says clearances are 'in Figure 4' (the clearance drawing is Figure 5); p. 16 says 'See page 12 for the fireplace minimum size' (Minimum Fireplace Dimensions are on p. 13). Not transcribed from drawings: the overall insert dimensions (Figure 2, p. 12), the minimum fireplace opening (Figure 3, p. 13; the text confirms only the 16" front / 8" side hearth extension), the ember-protection drawing (Figure 4, p. 14, whose labels read 'CAN: 20 1/4" / 610mm', 'USA: 18 1/4"', 'CAN 18" / 406mm', 'USA: 16"' and are not explained by the text; note 18" is paired with 406mm there but with 457 MM on the label), the 34 3/8" / 840mm value in Figure 5 (p. 15), the wiring diagram (p. 20) and the firebrick layout and brick sizes (pp. 23-25). Surround sizes are given as A / B exactly as the p. 12 table prints them; A and B are defined only on the drawing. Baffle-to-supply-tube gasket prt#80000365 (p. 11) does not appear in the parts list (p. 26), which has 80000356 'Gasket, 2" Baffle Tube, 10 pack' and 80002359 'Tube Air Box Gasket'; shown as printed in step 4. Warranty heading reads 'LTD Lifetime Coverage (10 years)'; shown as printed. EPA output appears two ways on p. 3: 13,500 to 23,200 Btu/hr (rating statement) and 13,494 to 23,186 btu/hr (table); treated as rounding, both shown in specEff, not flagged as a conflict. The manual does not state weight, firebox volume, heating area, maximum cordwood BTU, glass viewing area, blower cfm or combustion type, so those catalog fields were not checked (efficiency 72% HHV, 1.9 g/hr, 6" flue and EPA 23,200 Btu/hr agree). The catalog marks the model not for sale in the USA, but this manual carries USA-specific instructions (UL-1777 liner, direct flue connection permitted only in the USA, 16" US ember protection). Wood appliance: no gas-smell block, no ignition system, no code table (codes empty). Faults are from the p. 22 troubleshooting chart. No French-only or scrambled text needed translating (the rating label is bilingual; English used). Pages 29-31 are blank.
